# MM-P3-L2-SB01 Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01

Scope
This document defines routine maintenance tasks for the Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet EQ-P3-L2-SB01. It covers inspection, wear components replacement, media top-up, and mechanical fastener verification required to maintain safe and effective operation. Refer to ECN-2026-019 for change history and configuration baseline.

Tools
- Adjustable lifting strap and hoist suitable for cabinet access
- Torque wrench calibrated per facility practice
- Hand tools and fastener access set compatible with cabinet hardware
- Personal protective equipment as specified in SOP-P3-L2-01 and SOP-P3-L2-05

Procedure
Perform maintenance only after isolation and lockout in accordance with SOP-P3-L2-01. Verify cabinet is depressurized and power is isolated. Inspect cabinet interior for liner wear and foreign material. Remove worn liner panels following removal sequence in the cabinet access procedure in SOP-P3-L2-05. When reinstalling liner panels, clean mating surfaces and clamp panels to prevent movement during torqueing.

Fastener verification: tighten blast wheel liner bolts to the specified torque. The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m. Use a calibrated torque wrench and apply torque in a cross pattern to distribute load evenly.

Shot media: check media quality and contamination. Replenish media when level and performance indicate attrition. The shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours. Record media additions in the maintenance log and dispose of contaminated media per SOP-P3-L2-05.

Finalize maintenance by securing access panels and restoring normal energy following SOP-P3-L2-01. Run a verification cycle to confirm blast pattern and cabinet integrity before returning to production.

Acceptance criteria
- Liner panels secure with blast wheel liner bolts torqued to 100 N·m.  
- No visible cracks, distortions, or loose components inside the cabinet after maintenance.  
- Shot media level and condition meet operational requirements following the shot media top-up interval of 40 hours and documentation completed in the maintenance log.  
- Post-maintenance verification cycle demonstrates acceptable blast performance.  

Related documents: ECN-2026-019, SOP-P3-L2-01, SOP-P3-L2-05
